incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency > 2s for streaming API (region: us-west-2). Auto-threshold tripped at 2026-03-15T02:10:56Z :rotating_light:

incident-bot: metrics snapshot: p50=120ms p95=780ms p99=2.3s error_rate=0.6% impacted_routes=[/v1/stream, /v1/chat]

sre-oncall: seeing the same in dashboard. tail latency jump around 02:08 UTC. Starting triage.

alex.g: I just pulled logs, lots of 504s from streaming proxy toward kv-prefetch service.

maria_p: are we mid-rollout of any prefix-hash change? I remember a small rollout earlier today.

eng-runtime: yes — we rolled prefix-hash v3 -> v4 to 20% at 01:45 UTC (canary). It changes key salting for cache namespaces.

sre-oncall: OK let's correlate. Querying cache hitrate for affected shards...

sre-oncall: Query: select sum(hits)/sum(requests) from kv_prefetch where namespace in ('streaming','chat') and ts > now() - 1h

sre-oncall: result: hitrate dropped from 92% -> 47% starting ~01:47 UTC. That's correlated with the rollout.

product-ops: customer-facing impact? Support just flagged increased timeouts for a few key accounts.

support-lead: confirmed: 3 enterprise customers reported degraded streaming (buffers stalled), one escalated to SEV2. Tracing shows repeated cache misses causing origin fetch fallback.

eng-runtime: probable cause: prefix-hash change produced mismatched salt keys; clients hitting nodes that still expect old prefixes. We didn't warm new prefixes; fallback to origin increases tail.

alex.g: logs from kv-prefetch:
```
2026-03-15T01:48:02Z prefetched_key=abc123 ns=streaming hit=false route=/v1/stream fetch_ms=1200
2026-03-15T01:48:03Z salting_check=fail old_prefix=0x4f new_prefix=0xa1
```

eng-runtime: can reproduce locally with a small traffic replay. On nodes with v4 prefix parsing, existing caches look like miss.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback prefix-hash rollout to 0% 2) enable sticky routing to route traffic to v3 nodes 3) ramp up in-memory warmers to prefill v4 prefixes (slower) 4) increase stream timeouts (band-aid). Thoughts?

maria_p: rollback seems safest for customer impact. Are there safety checks that could break other things?

eng-runtime: rollback is supported and quick from the control plane. Risk: small window where v4 clients receive different responses but traffic is mostly server-side. I recommend rollback + coordinated warmup if we reattempt.

product-ops: agree rollback, tell support to notify customers. We'll prepare a status update.

sre-oncall: executing rollback now. 

ops-bot: @eng-runtime deploy rollback started: rollout-config prefix-hash:v4 -> v3 @ 1748124000 by sre-oncall

eng-runtime: monitoring cache hitrate + p99.

sre-oncall: metrics: 02:12 UTC p99 down to 1.1s (was 2.3s). cache hitrate climbing to ~85% on streaming namespace.

incident-bot: EVENT: rollback completed across 100% traffic at 02:14:08Z.

support-lead: SEV2 customer reported streams recovering. Sending interim note.

alex.g: root cause notes: missing cross-compatibility for prefix salts + no prefill for new salted namespace. We should add a canary warmup job and a checklist for prefix rollouts.

maria_p: capturing customer impact: ~4 customers affected intermittently, estimated 30m of degraded streaming in peak window. Logging for billing affected? support-lead: no billing change, only latency/errors.

eng-runtime: followups: - add prefill job that runs during prefix changes - add automated hitrate anomaly guard to abort rollout if hitrate delta > 15% within 10m - update runbook for rollback steps and status messages

product-ops: I'll draft the incident summary and external customer note.

sre-oncall: handing off to night oncall @maria_p. Please continue monitoring p95/p99 and watch the streaming proxy queue depth. If p99 > 1.5s for 10m, escalate to eng-runtime.

maria_p: ack takeover. I've got dashboards pinned and will watch alert channel.

ops-bot: @maria_p Oncall assignment changed: nights-sre (rotation) active until 1748170000.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated): root cause: prefix-hash rollout induced cache namespace mismatch -> cache miss surge -> origin fallbacks -> tail latency. Mitigation: rollback to v3.

support-lead: support notify sent to impacted customers with remediation ETA and postmortem promise.

alex.g: adding to postmortem: include instr to run prefills, add canary abort condition, run a small offline compatibility test between hash versions.

maria_p: leaving a short handoff note: p99 currently ~450ms, no ongoing errors. Will monitor for 2 hours then close monitoring.

eng-runtime: thanks all, will follow up tomorrow with a patch to add the automated hitrate guard.

product-ops: thanks team. prepping internal retrospective doc. :white_check_mark:
